rules.statement: In a test project, when a test asserts that a filter excludes some kind of item, make the fixture actually produce such an item and assert it appears upstream of the filter, so a regression of the filter fails the test.
rules.why: If the fixture never produces the excluded case, the assertion passes whether or not the filter works, and a regression would go unnoticed.
rules.check: Look for tests asserting an output lists only certain items after a filter; verify the fixture creates an item the filter must remove and that a separate assertion confirms that item was actually encountered.

rules.statement: In a test project, give each distinct skip or graceful-exit branch of a script its own fixture and assertions (exit code and skip reason), not just one sibling branch.
rules.why: An untested skip branch can regress into an error, for example failing CI in shallow clones or unrelated histories, with nothing catching it.
rules.check: When a script has several conditions that lead to a skip (for example missing remote ref vs. no merge base), check that tests cover each one, asserting success exit and the specific skip message.

rules.statement: Don't ask a test suite to dot-source or import another suite's shared fixture file just to reuse a small helper (such as a few-line git wrapper); suites keeping their own copy is intentional.
rules.why: Each suite should run on its own, and pulling in another suite's fixtures couples unrelated suites for a trivial helper.
rules.check: Before reporting a duplicated small helper in a test suite, check whether sibling suites follow the same per-suite copy pattern and whether the shared file belongs to a different suite group; if so, don't report it.
